He pulled her out of the rubble when she was ten. Seventeen years later, he married her.
Sichuan, May twelfth, two thousand eight. A magnitude eight earthquake.
In Qingchuan county, a two-storey building collapses. A ten-year-old girl, Liu Ximei, is trapped inside.
A young soldier, Liang Zhibin, twenty-two, digs with his team for hours, and carries her out.
What she remembers most: his hands. Covered in dirt, and warm.
Then they lose contact. For twelve years.
Twenty twenty. Changsha. Liu, now twenty-two, is having dinner with her parents.
Her mother looks at a man at the next table and says: he looks like Soldier Liang.
It is him. He doesn't recognise her.
At first he treats her like a little sister. The age gap worries him.
But they keep talking. And she tells him how she feels.
He says: saving her was my duty. Loving her comes from my heart.
